messages:
incident-bot: ALERT 2026-03-14T18:00Z — Elevated 504 gateway timeouts and 5xx errors observed from ap-northeast (apn1). Paging SRE oncall. :rotating_light:

sarah: I’m oncall. seeing timeout spike from ingress-apn1 -> model-svc clusters. 504s at ~25% of requests. dashboards: ingress_errors P95=24% across apn1.

lee: logs: nginx upstream timed out errors from ingress pods and repeated `grpc: deadline exceeded`. LB shows healthy targets but backend not responding timely.

priya: customer impact: 14 tenants affected with increased error rates; 3 customers reporting timeouts. marking incident P1 for apn1. updating status page.

tom: quick checks:
```
# ingress pods
kubectl -n infra get pods -l app=ingress-nginx --context=cluster-apn1 -o wide
# check events
kubectl --context=cluster-apn1 get events --sort-by=.lastTimestamp | tail -n 50
```

nate: I'm seeing a flood of kube-apiserver 429s in controller-manager logs. HorizontalPodAutoscaler scaling events are being throttled. That would explain worker pools not scaling to absorb load.

priya: Confirmed: HPA didn't create new replicas; model-workers remain at target but CPU pressure high and pod restarts increasing.

ops-oncall: network telemetry shows SYN-retries and many half-open connections on edge nodes; possible ephemeral port exhaustion on the NAT proxies.

infra-bot: collection started: /incidents/apn1/1952340001/ (metrics, pod logs, kernel, tcpdump).

sarah: initial mitigation proposal: 1) shift new traffic gradually from apn1 -> us-west2 (start with 15%) 2) restart ingress controllers one-by-one to clear stuck connections 3) bump conntrack and ephemeral port range on edge nodes 4) scale up a warm burst pool in us-west2 and enable routing override 5) rate-limit non-critical background traffic in apn1.

lee: taking ingress restarts now with 20s stagger.

# after restarts
lee: ingress restarts done. saw immediate drop in connection queue length. 504s dropped to ~18% from 25%. but still above baseline.

nate: executing routing override: 
```
infra-route set --from=ap-northeast --to=us-west2 --weight=15 --reason="apn1 ingress timeouts"
```

infra-bot: ACTION: routing override applied by nate at 18:07 UTC. Monitoring will report in 60s.

priya: statuspage updated: https://status.redwood.example/incidents/APN1-2026-03-14 "Partial failover to US-West for new sessions. Mitigations in progress."

tom: additional observation: model-worker pods show OOMKilled for a quantized model variant recently deployed in apn1 at 17:45 UTC. rolling revert to previous model image to free memory.

sarah: rolling revert started: 
```
kubectl -n models set image deployment/model-worker model-worker=registry.redwood/repo/model-worker:v2.3.8 --context=cluster-apn1
```

lee: revert completed on 60% of replicas; memory pressure dropped. connection resets reduced. 504s now ~9% in apn1.

nate: increased routing weight to 45%. us-west2 absorbing more new sessions. apn1 504s down to 4%. overall p95 latency back near baseline.

ops-oncall: applied transient sysctl changes to edge nodes: `net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=200000` and expanded `tcp_tw_reuse=1`. Monitoring for side effects.

priya: customer comms: preparing email to affected tenants, will send after mitigation stabilizes.

tom: we still need to address API-server throttling root cause. suspect control-plane load from a runaway informer or controller. scheduling deeper controller-manager profiling.

sarah: on-call handoff plan: I will run the emergency window until 19:00 UTC, then handoff to tom for post-incident work and RCA.

infra-bot: artifacts uploaded: s3://redwood-incident-archives/APN1/1952340001/ (metrics, logs, core dumps, tcpdumps).

priya: METRICS UPDATE 18:22 UTC — apn1 5xx = 3.7% (baseline 0.6%), us-west2 p95 increased by 0.3s but within SLA.

cs-bot: Drafted customer message queued for 18:30 UTC: "We experienced increased timeouts in APAC. We enacted partial failover to a secondary region; services are stabilizing. Detailed report will follow."

nate: added a temporary rate-limit rule for crawler/ingest jobs in apn1 (rl-crawler-apn1 -> reduce by 70%). Freed ~15% capacity on ingress.

lee: verifying HPA event logs: controller-manager shows sustained burst of list/watch calls from telemetry-agent v0.9.7 between 17:40-17:58 UTC. we've throttled the agent by deploying v0.9.8 (with reduced resync).

tom: controller-manager CPU usage dropping; HPA now able to push new replicas when needed. Good to monitor for 1h.

priya: INCIDENT STATUS: mitigated at 18:25 UTC. Partial failover remains for new sessions; apn1 handling existing sessions. Postmortem owner: tom.

sarah: noted action items: investigate telemetry agent regression (TLM-5012), add control-plane headroom during peak windows, add automation for regional pre-warm, update routing fallback runbook, and revert transient sysctl after full proof.

ops-oncall: scheduling follow-up: kernel tuning review and NAT proxy scaling (INF-8340).

cs-bot: Customer notifications sent at 18:30 UTC.

tom: I'll draft the incident report and schedule the postmortem review tomorrow 10:00 UTC. thanks for fast coordinated ops. :thumbsup:"
